blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — intrahospital transport of a critically ill client
stem: A critically ill client must be transported from the ICU to another department for a procedure. Which plan best supports safe intrahospital transport?

options.A: Coordinate the transport in advance and use monitoring, equipment, and accompanying personnel matched to the client's current critical-care needs.
options.B: Send the client without monitoring when the destination is nearby, provided the most recent vital signs were stable immediately before departure.
options.C: Leave emergency and monitoring equipment on the ICU because the receiving department becomes responsible once the client leaves the unit.
options.D: Use an available escort without critical-care training when the transport is brief and the receiving department has emergency equipment ready.

rationale: A is correct. SCCM/ACCM transport guidance calls for a formalized process addressing pretransport coordination and communication, qualified transport personnel, appropriate transport equipment, monitoring during transport, and documentation. A 2025 critical-care position statement likewise emphasizes thorough assessment and preparation of the patient, staff, and equipment throughout intrahospital transport. Proximity or a single stable vital-sign snapshot does not remove the need for appropriate monitoring, equipment, and personnel during transport.
educational_objective: Plan intrahospital transport of a critically ill client using pretransport coordination plus monitoring, equipment, and personnel matched to current clinical needs.
source_organization: American College of Critical Care Medicine / Society of Critical Care Medicine (SCCM); Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine (ISCCM); NCSBN
source_document_title: Guidelines for the inter- and intrahospital transport of critically ill patients; Position Statement of ISCCM on Intrahospital Transport of Critically Ill Patients; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: SCCM/ACCM 2004; ISCCM 2025; currentness rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026

ISCCM 2025 abstract: thorough assessment and preparation of patients, staff, and equipment throughout transport; recommendations cover pre-, intra-, and post-transport safety.
source_claim_supported: Authoritative critical-care guidance supports organized pretransport planning, appropriate monitoring/equipment, and trained personnel throughout intrahospital transport.

pdf_visual_verification: PASS — official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; transport claims rely on PubMed-indexed critical-care guidance.

option_audit.A: Correct; matches organized preparation, monitoring, equipment, and personnel requirements.
option_audit.B: Plausible proximity shortcut but brief distance and stable pretransport vitals do not remove monitoring needs.
option_audit.C: Plausible transfer-of-responsibility misconception but transport itself requires appropriate monitoring and equipment.
option_audit.D: Plausible staffing shortcut but critically ill transport requires personnel matched to patient needs.

cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options are similar in detail and clinical plausibility; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
